description: Schema: word lists, categories, user words with copy-on-write, API key storage, media assets
steps: Create `word_lists` table: id, owner_id (null = system), name, description, language_from, language_to, is_public, created_at, updated_at

Create `word_categories` table: id, list_id (FK word_lists), name, position (integer for drag-drop ordering), is_system (boolean — true for seeded categories, false for user-created), created_at. System categories seeded for default lists. Users can create custom categories scoped to their own lists only

Create `word_list_items` table: id, list_id (FK word_lists), category_id (FK word_categories), canonical_word_id (FK words, nullable — reference to original if copy-on-write), position (integer within category), text_known (required), text_target (nullable — null until translated, but required for card to function in learning view), translation_status ('manual' | 'pending' | 'translated' | 'failed'), audio_asset_id (FK media_assets, nullable — optional, card works without audio), audio_status ('none' | 'pending' | 'ready' | 'failed'), notes (nullable), created_at, updated_at

Copy-on-write applies to word TEXT and POSITION only. When user copies/edits a word from a curated list, create a new word_list_item on user's own list with its own text_known, text_target, position, category. But audio_asset_id is a SHARED REFERENCE — the copied item points to the same media_asset row as the original. No audio bytes are ever duplicated. If user later regenerates audio (e.g. with ElevenLabs), a new media_asset is created and the user's item re-points to it, but the original shared asset remains for other users. Set canonical_word_id pointing to the original for traceability

Create `media_assets` table: id, content_hash (unique — dedup key and the cornerstone of audio sharing), storage_type ('arweave' | 'r2'), storage_ref (arweave TX ID or R2 key), media_type ('audio'), language, text_reference, provider ('google_tts' | 'elevenlabs'), size_bytes, created_at. This is a SHARED POOL — many word_list_items across many users point to the same media_asset row. Assets are never deleted when a single user removes a word; cleanup (if ever needed) is a background job that checks for orphaned assets with zero references

Create `user_api_keys` table: id, user_id, provider ('openrouter' | 'elevenlabs'), encrypted_key (AES-256 with APP_ENCRYPTION_SECRET), created_at. Never return key to client after storage. Show last 4 chars only in UI

Update `user_progress`: add word_list_item_id FK. Progress is per (user, word_list_item). On word removal: set archived_at timestamp, preserve all SR state, hide from stats. On re-add: match by text_known — if archived entry exists, restore it (clear archived_at, keep stage/nextDueAt)

Minimum viable card rule: word_list_item appears in learning view only if both text_known AND text_target are present. Items with null text_target are shown in editor as 'needs translation' but excluded from word stream

Create `user_list_subscriptions` table: id, user_id (FK users), list_id (FK word_lists), subscribed_at. Unique on (user_id, list_id). Tracks which curated/public lists a user is subscribed to. Subscription triggers copy-on-write of items into user's own list

Add indexes: (list_id, category_id, position) on word_list_items, (content_hash) unique on media_assets, (user_id, provider) unique on user_api_keys, (user_id, word_list_item_id) on user_progress, (user_id, list_id) unique on user_list_subscriptions
Write Drizzle migration, run pnpm db:generate && pnpm db:migrate

description: Migrate existing data to list-based schema without breaking spaced repetition
steps: Run pnpm db:backup before any migration work
Create system-owned word_list: 'Default Vietnamese–Czech' with is_public=true
Convert existing category data into word_categories rows with is_system=true, position matching current order

Convert existing words table rows into word_list_items on the default list, preserving category assignment and position. Set canonical_word_id=null (these ARE the canonical words). Set translation_status='manual', audio_status based on whether audio exists
Map existing user_progress entries to new word_list_item_ids via (text_known + text_target) matching. Preserve stage, nextDueAt, all SR state. Log any unmatched entries for manual review
Map existing user_memory_hooks to new word_list_item references
Map existing user_category_filters to category_id references on new schema

Auto-subscribe all existing users to the default system list via user_list_subscriptions (see user_list_subscriptions table in data-model). Copy all default list word_list_items into each user's own list (copy-on-write for text/position — gives every user full edit capability from day one). Copied items inherit the SAME audio_asset_id as the original — no audio duplication. Many user items → one shared media_asset row
Update useWordStream: source words from user's own word_list_items (where text_known AND text_target are both present). Same due/new/settling bucket logic
Update minigames: replace anchorOriginalIndex with word_list_item.id as stable anchor
Write assertion tests: for each existing user, verify word stream output is identical pre/post migration (same words, same order, same SR state)
Keep old /api/words endpoint as read-only during transition, remove after verification

description: API routes for list and category management
steps: GET /api/lists — return lists available to user: own lists + public browseable. Include item count, language pair, category count
POST /api/lists — create new user list (name, language_from, language_to). Auto-create with is_public=false, owner_id=current user
GET /api/lists/[id] — return list with categories and word_list_items, ordered by category.position then item.position. Auth: owner or public
PUT /api/lists/[id] — update metadata (name, description, is_public). Owner only
DELETE /api/lists/[id] — delete list. Archive all related user_progress (set archived_at, don't delete). Owner only
GET /api/lists/[id]/categories — return categories for list, ordered by position
POST /api/lists/[id]/categories — create new user-defined category. Scoped to user's own list only (reject if list.owner_id != current user). Set position to max+1
PUT /api/lists/[id]/categories — update category order (array of { id, position }). Supports drag-and-drop reorder. Owner only
DELETE /api/lists/[id]/categories/[catId] — delete category. Move contained words to an 'Uncategorized' default category, or reject if category not empty (decide in implementation)

description: API routes for the textarea word editing wizard: diff, preview, confirm
steps: PUT /api/lists/[id]/categories/[catId]/items/preview — accepts { lines: string[], input_language: 'known' | 'target' }. Lines are one word/phrase per line. Diffs against current items in that category. Returns { added: string[], removed: { id, text_known, text_target }[], reordered: { id, text, from_pos, to_pos }[], unchanged: number }

Diff algorithm: match by exact text in the specified input_language field. Normalize: trim whitespace, collapse multiple spaces, case-insensitive comparison. Same text = same item (possibly repositioned). New text = addition. Missing text = removal
Edge case handling: duplicate lines → reject with error listing the duplicate texts and their line numbers. Empty lines → strip silently. Max 500 items per category → warn if exceeded

POST /api/lists/[id]/categories/[catId]/items/confirm — applies the previewed diff. Removals: set archived_at on user_progress for removed items, delete word_list_items. Additions: create word_list_items — if input_language='known', set text_known and text_target=null (needs translation); if input_language='target', set text_target and text_known=null. Reorders: update position values
For order-only or removal-only changes (no new words): confirm completes the wizard immediately, no further steps needed. Return { completed: true, needs_translation: false }
For changes with new words: return { completed: false, needs_translation: true, pending_items: [...] } — client proceeds to translation step

description: Wizard step: generate translations for new/edited words. Skippable — user can manually enter translations instead
steps: After confirm returns pending_items, client shows translation step. User can choose: 'Auto-translate' (API) or 'I'll translate myself' (manual entry for all words)

DB dedup lookup first: for each pending item, search all word_list_items and canonical words for matching text in same language pair. If match found, copy the translation and set translation_status='manual'. Report reuse count to user

POST /api/translate/batch — accepts { items: { id, text, from_lang, to_lang }[], provider: 'google' | 'openrouter' }. Returns { results: { id, translated_text, status: 'ok' | 'error', error?: string }[] }

Google Cloud Translation API v2: server-side GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_API_KEY. Batch up to 128 strings per request. Track daily usage in DB (translations_today counter per user). MVP limit: 500 translations/user/day

OpenRouter integration (BYOK only): decrypt user's stored key server-side. Translation system prompt: precise, request single translation per word, structured JSON response. Batch up to 50 words per prompt

UI: two-column editable table — known language | target language. API results pre-filled. Every cell editable (user can correct any translation). Failed rows highlighted with retry button. Provider selector shown only if user has BYOK key stored
Manual mode: if user chose 'I'll translate myself', show same two-column table but target column is empty and editable. No API calls made
Confirm translations: update word_list_items with final text_target values. Set translation_status='translated' or 'manual'. Items now meet minimum viable card requirement (both texts present)
Skip entirely: user can skip this step and return later. Items remain with text_target=null, excluded from learning view until translated

description: Wizard step: generate pronunciation audio. Fully optional — cards work without audio
steps: After translations confirmed (or if user entered target language directly), client shows audio step. User can: generate audio, or skip entirely

DB dedup check (PRIMARY PATH — most words should resolve here): for each word, compute hash(text_target + language + provider). Check media_assets for matching content_hash. If found, link existing media_asset to word_list_item via audio_asset_id — zero generation, zero storage, just a FK reference. Report reuse count to user (e.g. '38 of 42 words already have audio'). Only words with no matching media_asset proceed to generation

POST /api/audio/generate/batch — accepts { items: { id, text, language }[], provider: 'google_tts' | 'elevenlabs' }. Process in small parallel batches (3–5 concurrent). Returns per-item: { id, audio_url, status: 'ok' | 'error', error?: string }
Google Cloud TTS: server-side GOOGLE_TTS_API_KEY. MP3 output. MVP limit: 200 generations/user/day
ElevenLabs (BYOK only): decrypt user's key via Cloudflare Worker proxy (key never on Next.js server). User selects voice in settings. Higher quality output
Storage: upload to Arweave via ArDrive Turbo SDK. Store arweave_tx_id + content_hash in media_assets. Fallback: if Arweave upload fails, store in Cloudflare R2, mark storage_type='r2'
Update word_list_items: set audio_asset_id and audio_status='ready' for successes, 'failed' for errors

Playback UI: word list with per-word play button. Currently-playing word highlighted visually (e.g. accent border or background pulse). 'Play all' button: sequential playback with ~1.5s gap between words. 'Play edited only' button: plays only newly generated/changed audio. User can pause at any time

Per-word regenerate: click regenerate on any word. If user has ElevenLabs BYOK, option to regenerate with ElevenLabs even if original was Google TTS. Regeneration ALWAYS creates a new media_asset row (different content_hash) and re-points only this user's word_list_item.audio_asset_id. The original shared media_asset is never modified or deleted — other users' items still reference it. Old asset remains in media_assets for anyone else using it

For words that already had audio (editing existing words, step 2 from user flow): show existing audio with play button + option to regenerate with ElevenLabs if BYOK. No generation needed unless user requests it
Skip: 'Skip audio' button available at all times. Cards work without audio. User can return to generate audio later from list/category settings
Confirm & finish: wizard complete. All changes live. Trigger word stream invalidation in AppStateContext

description: Desktop editing page: list browser, category manager, textarea editor, wizard steps
steps: Create /lists page (desktop only). Left sidebar: list of available lists — user's own list(s) at top, curated/public lists below. Click to select active list for viewing/editing. Toggle switches on curated lists for subscribe/unsubscribe

Main area: selected list content. Collapsible category sections ordered by category.position. Each section header: category name, word count, drag handle for reorder. Drag-and-drop on category headers syncs with PUT /api/lists/[id]/categories
'+ Add category' button at bottom of category list. Creates user-scoped category via POST /api/lists/[id]/categories
Click category → expands to show words as simple list (text_known column, text_target column if available, audio indicator icon). 'Edit words' button on each category
'Edit words' opens textarea panel: pre-filled with one word per line. Input language toggle at top: 'Entering words in: [Czech | Vietnamese]'. Free editing — add, remove, reorder lines

'Preview changes' button: calls PUT /api/lists/[id]/categories/[catId]/items/preview. Shows diff panel: added (green), removed (red), reordered (with arrows showing position change), unchanged count. Summary line: 'X added, Y removed, Z reordered, W unchanged'
'Confirm changes' button: calls POST confirm endpoint. If order/removal only → wizard done, show success. If new words → proceeds to translation step

Translation step UI: two-column editable table. Provider selector (Google default, OpenRouter if BYOK set). 'Auto-translate' and 'I'll translate myself' buttons. Per-row edit, per-row retry on failure. 'Confirm translations' proceeds to audio step (or finishes if user skips audio)

Audio step UI: word list with play buttons. Currently-playing word highlighted (accent border or background pulse animation). 'Play all' / 'Play edited' / single play. Per-word regenerate button with provider choice. Progress bar during batch generation. 'Skip audio' and 'Confirm & finish' buttons

Settings section (accessible from /lists page or main app settings): BYOK API key management. Add/remove keys for OpenRouter and ElevenLabs. Keys masked (last 4 chars). ElevenLabs voice selector (fetched from API if key present)
Mobile viewport: show read-only list view — categories and word counts, expandable to see words. No editing capability. Banner: 'Edit your word list on desktop'
On wizard completion: invalidate AppStateContext cached word data, trigger useWordStream refresh. Learning view immediately reflects changes

description: Arweave storage, R2 CDN cache, Cloudflare Worker proxy for media and BYOK key safety
steps: Create Cloudflare Worker: wordlink-media-proxy. Env vars: APP_ENCRYPTION_SECRET (for BYOK key decryption), ARWEAVE_WALLET_JWK, R2 bucket binding
Worker route POST /upload: receives audio bytes + content_hash + metadata. Uploads to Arweave via ArDrive Turbo SDK. Returns arweave_tx_id. On Arweave failure: falls back to R2 upload, returns r2_key
Worker route GET /audio/:hash: serves audio. Check R2 cache first → if miss, fetch from Arweave gateway → cache result in R2 (30 day TTL) → return audio. Set Cache-Control headers for browser caching

Worker route POST /elevenlabs-proxy: receives encrypted_key blob + text + voice_id. Decrypts key using APP_ENCRYPTION_SECRET. Calls ElevenLabs TTS API. Returns audio bytes. Key never logged, never stored, never leaves Worker memory
R2 bucket: 'wordlink-media'. Keys are content_hash values. Lifecycle rule: delete objects not accessed in 90 days (they can be re-fetched from Arweave)
Arweave budget: project-owned wallet for MVP. Track daily upload bytes in DB. MVP limit: 10MB/day total across all users. Display remaining quota in audio step UI
Prefetch in learning view: on page load, identify next 10 due words with audio. Inject <link rel='prefetch'> tags for their audio URLs pointing at the Worker GET endpoint
Fallback chain: browser cache → R2 via Worker → Arweave gateway. If all fail, card renders without audio (graceful degradation, no error shown to user)

description: Subscribe to curated lists, toggle on/off, multi-list learning
steps: Toggle UI on /lists page sidebar: each curated/public list has a toggle switch. Toggle on = subscribe, toggle off = unsubscribe

On subscribe (POST /api/lists/[id]/subscribe): copy-on-write all items from curated list into user's own list — copies text_known, text_target, position, category. audio_asset_id is copied AS-IS (shared reference to the same media_asset, no audio duplication). User can edit text freely; audio stays shared until user explicitly regenerates. Create user_progress entries for all copied items. Mark subscription in user_list_subscriptions

On unsubscribe (DELETE /api/lists/[id]/subscribe): archive user_progress for items that came from this list (set archived_at). Remove copied items from user's list (or mark inactive). Progress preserved, hidden from stats, restorable

Multi-list learning: if user subscribes to multiple lists, their own list contains the union of copied items. useWordStream draws from user's single list (which contains copies from all subscribed lists + user's own additions). Dedup by canonical_word_id — if same word copied from 2 curated lists, keep the one with higher progress

Curated list updates: when list owner adds new words, existing subscribers do NOT auto-receive them (since we use copy-on-write, subscriber's copy is independent). Show notification: 'List X has 5 new words since you subscribed — add them?' User can pull updates explicitly
Future: fork list (explicit full copy with editing UI). Defer to post-MVP
Future: smart merge (dedup across lists, resolve order). Defer to post-MVP

description: Phased build sequence — each phase is independently shippable and testable
steps: Phase 1 — Schema + Migration + Basic Editor: data-model, migration, api-lists, api-editing, editing-ui (textarea + diff/confirm only). New words require manual text_target entry in editor. No translation/audio API integration. Ship and verify: SR works, existing progress intact, editor diff/confirm works, categories reorderable. This is the foundation everything else builds on

Phase 2 — Translation Pipeline: translation-step + editing-ui translation step. Google Translate with server-side key. BYOK OpenRouter support. DB dedup before API calls. Manual entry always available as fallback

Phase 3 — Audio Pipeline: audio-step + audio-infrastructure + editing-ui audio step. Google TTS default, ElevenLabs BYOK via CF Worker proxy. Arweave + R2 storage. Content-addressed dedup. Play all / play edited / single play with visual highlight. Fully skippable
Phase 4 — List Subscription: list-subscription. Toggle curated lists. Copy-on-write on subscribe. Multi-list dedup in word stream. Progress archival on unsubscribe. Update notifications
Phase 5 — Scale + Polish: rate limiting hardening, batch job queue for large translation/audio jobs, fork/combine lists, mobile read-only improvements, Arweave BYOK wallet support
